text: Spend like you normally do. Stoke finds the recurring transactions in your history, then projects each account forward, day by day, so you know what you can spend without keeping a budget. Three steps from sign-up to a forecast that updates as you spend. Link a bank in seconds, or hand-enter accounts and transactions yourself. Either way, it feeds the same forecast. Paychecks, rent, subscriptions, and bills are picked out of your history and grouped. Anything we miss, you categorize once with a rule that runs on future transactions too. The forecast shows when bills land, what your buffer looks like, and whether rent will clear Friday. Adjust any projected item and the line moves. The ledger and the forecast are the same data, day by day. Cash leaves when the card is paid, not at each swipe. See where your money stands today — and where it's headed. Connect Claude, ChatGPT, or another MCP-capable assistant to your Stoke data. Ask what you can afford, then have it categorize transactions or draft a plan. Hand-entry is on the house. Pay for bank sync, and for AI access if you want it. Bank credentials are the most sensitive thing you'll hand an app. Here's how we handle them, and the rest of your data. The same connection Chime and Robinhood use. We never see or store your bank login, and access is read-only — Stoke can't move money. Bank access tokens and account numbers are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they're stored, and everything travels over TLS. Sign in with a passkey or a one-time email link — there's no password to leak. We make money from subscriptions, not from your data — it's never sold or used for advertising. Cancel and your data stays put. Delete and it's gone for good. Bank sync runs through Plaid, which reaches most US and Canadian banks but not all. Any account it can't reach, you can hand-enter, and it sits in the same forecast as your synced accounts. Yes. A card purchase shows up in your spending the day you swipe. Cash leaves when you pay the card, so the forecast projects each card's payment on its due date, out of the account that pays it. Yes. Stoke doesn't include a chatbot. Pro adds an MCP connection from an AI app you already use — Claude, ChatGPT, or another that supports MCP — to your Stoke data, so it can read your forecast and act on it. It answers questions about your spending, recurring bills, and projected balances. With write access it can also categorize transactions, create rules, and build plans. You pick read-only or read and write when you connect, and can revoke access at any time from Settings. You're moved to the free plan. Your accounts, transactions, and forecast all stay — only live bank sync stops. To turn it back on, re-subscribe and reconnect your bank through Plaid. Everything goes — accounts, transactions, the forecast, and any linked bank connections. Deletion is final; we don't keep a copy.
